classification.difficultyReason: Assemble whole sides from labelled segments, compare ratios about the common angle, then follow the supplied similarity-to-parallelism proof pattern.

content.prompt: In each part below, prove that $\triangle ABC$ is similar to $\triangle APQ$. Then prove that $PQ$ is parallel to $BC$.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle ABC with P on AB, Q on AC and internal segment PQ. Ordinary source-blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: A–P–B and A–Q–C are collinear; AP=5, PB=3, AQ=8, QC=4.8. No parallel marks or units are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens remain visible; no proof conclusions are drawn.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\sim\triangle APQ$ (SAS), since $\frac{AB}{AP}=\frac{AC}{AQ}=\frac{8}{5}$ and the included angle at $A$ is common.

$\angle APQ=\angle ABC$, so $PQ\parallel BC$ by equal corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=5+3=8\\AC&=8+4.8=12.8\\\frac{AB}{AP}&=\frac85\\\frac{AC}{AQ}&=\frac{12.8}{8}=\frac85\end{align*}$$
$\angle BAC=\angle PAQ$ (common angle). Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle APQ$ (SAS).

$\angle APQ=\angle ABC$ (matching angles of similar triangles). Since $A,P,B$ are collinear, these are corresponding angles for lines $PQ$ and $BC$. Hence $PQ\parallel BC$.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with horizontal AC, B above and slightly right of C, internal PQ, and an unnumbered common-angle arc at A. Ordinary source-blue strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: A–P–B and A–Q–C are collinear; AP=8, PB=2, AQ=6, QC=1½. No parallel marks or units are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens and the source angle cue remain visible; no proof conclusions are drawn.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\sim\triangle APQ$ (SAS), since $\frac{AB}{AP}=\frac{AC}{AQ}=\frac{5}{4}$ and the included angle at $A$ is common.

$\angle APQ=\angle ABC$, so $PQ\parallel BC$ by equal corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AB&=8+2=10\\AC&=6+1\frac12=\frac{15}{2}\\\frac{AB}{AP}&=\frac{10}{8}=\frac54\\\frac{AC}{AQ}&=\frac{15/2}{6}=\frac54\end{align*}$$
$\angle BAC=\angle PAQ$ (common angle). Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle APQ$ (SAS).

$\angle APQ=\angle ABC$ (matching angles of similar triangles). Since $A,P,B$ are collinear, these are corresponding angles for lines $PQ$ and $BC$. Hence $PQ\parallel BC$.
